title: Implement target-effective state and deterministic rule packets

scope.target: GitHub Issues #112 and #113; target-effective lifecycle, compact index, resolver, freshness/digest, and full-statement packets.

steps: Implement deterministic index and packet generation
Implement common resolver and fail-closed freshness states
validation: Manual stale, conflict, missing, and digest-mismatch scenario review
execution.last_completed_step: Defined target-owned effective-state and packet contracts, implemented deterministic packet build/resolve and staged publication, integrated lifecycle hooks and package reservations, and closed independent semantic/runtime review blockers through root read-back.
execution.next_action: Commit the RPB-003 checkpoint, then begin RPB-005 provider relocation and reference-in-place activation without changing target-owned configuration.

results.summary: Target repositories now have a template-only, target-owned effective-rule state, complete self-contained task packets, deterministic exact routing, authority/catalog/state/packet freshness binding, and a shared read-only resolver that fails closed without scanning Markdown or using framework defaults.
files_changed: effective-rule state/packet schemas and lifecycle references
shared resolver, candidate builder, staged writer, and target validation integration
package preservation, distribution, entrypoint, and representative GWT test source
results.residual_risk: No local tests or repository validation scripts ran by owner direction. Twelve profile documents remain explicitly unpacketized until stable identities are allocated; constraint tuning/waiver resolution remains fail-closed until stable constraint records exist. Multi-file publication is packets-first/state-last with in-process rollback, not cross-file crash atomicity; crash-mixed state cannot pass freshness checks.
